# Syncle

> Open-source, self-hosted database synchronization. Draw a bridge from a
> source database to one or more destinations and Syncle keeps them in sync —
> live via change data capture (CDC), polled via cursors, or as a one-shot
> backfill. PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite, MongoDB and Redis, any engine
> to any other, plus HTTP endpoints as destinations. MIT licensed.

Install with one command (requires Docker with Compose v2, and curl):

    curl -fsSL https://syncle.dev/install | sh -s -- up

## What it guarantees

- Idempotent upserts keyed by columns you choose: replays, retries and
  redeliveries never double-write.
- With CDC triggers, inserts, updates AND deletes propagate, each tagged with
  its operation. Watch triggers poll, so they detect new rows (and updates on
  a timestamp cursor) but not deletes.
- Missing destination tables are created from the source's shape, with types
  translated across engines.
- Columns can be mapped and renamed as rows cross.
- Interrupted jobs resume from their cursor instead of starting over.

## How a bridge fires

- Replay: one-shot stream of the source (initial backfill, migrations).
- Watch: cursor polling (auto-increment id, updated_at, or primary-key diff);
  works on every engine, including SQLite.
- CDC: real-time change capture — Postgres logical replication, MySQL binlog,
  MongoDB change streams, Redis keyspace notifications. SQLite has no change
  log, so it syncs by watch rather than CDC; Redis keyspace notifications are
  not durable, so events during downtime are lost.

## Key facts

- Self-hosted: no account and no third party in the data path.
- Stored connection credentials are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) with a key that
  never leaves the install.
- SSH tunnels reach databases on private networks.
- A lightweight alternative to Airbyte (no Kubernetes) and Debezium (no
  Kafka) for single-operator use.
